messages:
Sam W.: Observed pinned variant still receiving traffic after retire_at. Router didn't re-evaluate mid-session.

Aisha: paste manifest fragment?

Sam W.: {"model_id":"gpt-redwood-v2","variant":"f16-q4","pin":true,"retire_at":1706000000,"soft_deprecate":true}

Jun K.: We have two overlapping signals. Propose an explicit lifecycle enum instead of ad-hoc fields.

Toni: Draft schema idea: {"lifecycle":{"phase":"active|deprecated|draining|retired","effective_at":<ts>,"cache_ttl_s":<n>,"lease_s":<n>,"pin_scope":"none|tenant|system"}}

Aisha: Semantics we want: deprecated = no new auto-pins, allow existing sessions; draining = reject new sessions, honor leases/cache_ttl; retired = stop serving.

Sam W.: Control plane should issue short-lived lease tokens for pinned sessions so runtime can revoke mid-session. Back-compat: if lifecycle missing, treat retire_at as effective_at->retired.

ops-oncall: Ops runbook defaults: deprecated 48h, draining 12h, cache_ttl 24h for pinned sessions. Emergency force_retire allowed but requires RBAC + two-person approval and audit.

Toni: Action items: I'll open RFC patch with schema + runbook. Jun: add tests for state transitions. Ops: prepare emergency playbook.

Sam W.: Agreed decisions: lifecycle enum + effective_at, cache_ttl_s, lease_s, pin_scope, lease tokens, force_retire w/ audit, back-compat retire_at fallback.

Aisha: We'll include tenant-facing SLA language about how long tenant-scoped pins survive through draining.
